notes.title: A conversation between TAKUMI and Tetsuya Nomura
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/bf0b46349438c430535f8f22d93e01b678283853.jpg
NIS America releases REYNATIS for the Nintendo Switch™, PS5®, PS4® and Steam. The game is set in the year 2024 in Shibuya, Tokyo, where magic exists. The story follows a pair with very different positions and perspectives: a young wizard named Marin Kirizumi who longs for freedom, and Sari Nishijima, an M.E.A. officer who wishes to bring order to the world.

* This article was originally published on the NIS America website. You can find the original content at the following link: A conversation between REYNATIS Creative Producer TAKUMI and NEO: The World Ends With You's Tetsuya Nomura

This title, which has received much attention, has a star-studded staff including scenario writer Kazushige Nojima, music by Yoko Shimomura, and character visuals by Yusuke Naora.

Not only that, but REYNATIS, which shares its setting of Shibuya with Square Enix's action RPG series The World Ends With You (hereafter TWEWY), will have an in-game collaboration!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/cd671d50941bcc7d9c1c2d7483fb240733b20cd6.jpg
The collaboration begins with Marin picking up a certain badge and being transported to the Shibuya of NEO: The World Ends With You (hereafter NTWEWY). In order to escape, he has to participate in the Reapers' Game. Rindo and Shoka, as well as the Noise, from NTWEWY also appear, making for one very in-depth collaboration.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/23f62bd6ca374a3420e221a4e50bd3278383c974.jpg
To commemorate the upcoming launch of REYNATIS and this collaboration, Weekly Famitsu sat down with TAKUMI, Creative Producer for REYNATIS and Tetsuya Nomura, Creative Producer and Character Designer of the TWEWY series.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/9b59a632a3ba1ab052ab9e8fd6bf8165b1d8f502.jpg
Read on for more information about how this collaboration came to be, TAKUMI's respect for Tetsuya Nomura, and what both creators keep in mind when developing games.

TAKUMI
A game creator from FURYU. He serves as the Creative Producer for REYNATIS.

Tetsuya Nomura (hereafter Nomura)
Creative Producer and Character Designer for NEO: The World Ends With You. He joined Square in 1991, where he worked on the development of the Final Fantasy series and was the Character Designer for Final Fantasy VII. After, he worked as a main staff member on Final Fantasy VIII, Final Fantasy X, Final Fantasy X-2, and Final Fantasy XIII, among others. He is also the Creative Director of the Final Fantasy VII Remake project. Additionally, he is the Character Designer, Game Designer, and Director of the Kingdom Hearts series, which is co-produced with Disney. He has played a key role in many titles at Square Enix.

The collaboration born from TAKUMI's sincerity and respect toward Mr. Nomura
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— TAKUMI, in a previous interview, you said that REYNATIS was greatly influenced by the Final Fantasy and Kingdom Hearts series. You have a strong admiration for Mr. Nomura, so what was your impression when you first met him?

TAKUMI I had the impression he was super scary before we met, so I was very nervous. However, when I was actually able to speak with him, I found him easy to talk to.

Nomura Well, my personal "concept" is to be easily approachable.

—— Ahahaha. (sheepish laughter) How about you? What did you think when you first met TAKUMI, Mr. Nomura?

Nomura Mr. Nojima (Kazushige Nojima, the Scenario Writer for REYNATIS and many of Mr. Nomura's projects) had written about TAKUMI on X (formerly Twitter), so I had an idea of what he would be like. When I met him, my impression was that he was like other young, contemporary people.

—— That's true; he is young. Their [FURYU Corporation's] building company building is in Shibuya, and all of it is very stylish. What was your impression of TAKUMI's game, REYNATIS?

Nomura When I was approached about the collaboration, I took a look at the planning documents and thought, "He's really going for it." (laughs)

TAKUMI (strained laughter)

—— When they saw the initial trailer, I'm sure many gamers felt the same way. (laughs) "This reminds me of one of Mr. Nomura's games…"

Nomura But, checking out the story, I felt that he had truly devised his own world. I wondered how the story would play out being set in Shibuya.

[previewyoutube=ccKIyKoKjJY;full][/previewyoutube]

—— The setting for REYNATIS is Shibuya. Is part of the reason you made Shibuya the setting due to the TWEWY series?

TAKUMI Honestly, it wasn't. I think for players outside of Japan, the most recognizable place in Japan is the Shibuya Scramble Crossing, so I chose Shibuya as the setting.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/2b4fb791decfaf18150a99dfbf894889c4ab1c31.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/e8b34600c9cb67b75deaf5f9f5eb38507daa4b6d.jpg

—— I see. So, when did you first think up the idea for this collaboration?

TAKUMI At first, I didn't think it would be possible to do a collaboration for a console game with another company. But, while working on REYNATIS and looking at the in-game Shibuya, I remembered TWEWY… I thought, “It's the same setting, after all. A collaboration would be a lot of fun." So, fully expecting it to get shot down, I decided to bring it up.

Nomura Honestly, before even seeing the planning documents for REYNATIS, I thought, "There are other games that use Shibuya as a setting, so why TWEWY?" But, once I saw those design docs, I thought, "I get it now. This guy really likes TWEWY." (laughs)

—— It seems TAKUMI's passion for TWEWY is what led to this collaboration.

Nomura Yes. His proposal was very straightforward in terms of showing, "I really like your work!" The purity of that sentiment made me want to help out. He mustered up the courage to ask, and there aren't many young people who would do that, so I didn't want to take those feelings lightly.

When I was making Kingdom Hearts, I had to negotiate with Disney, as well as sound out Utada Hikaru for the main theme song. So, I thought it was great that there was this young creator coming at us confidently with a straightforward offer.

—— Ah, so you yourself have the experience of knocking on the doors of other companies, so you know how it feels. Including TWEWY, what do you like about Mr. Nomura's works, TAKUMI?

TAKUMI I like his world settings that are "fantasy, but set in the real world." Particularly, I'm really smitten with his portrayal of the darkness in people, as well as how cool people can be.

I've read many of his interviews, and in them, I really got the sense of how difficult it was to get the plan for Kingdom Hearts, as approved and as well as his enthusiasm, and his creative drive and way of thinking. Even through the interview, all this came through, and I was really taken with those things.

—— So, you were taken with his approach as a creator. What was the first game of his you played?

TAKUMI The first one was when I was in middle school, and it was the first Kingdom Hearts. After that, I played just about every game that Mr. Nomura worked on. I particularly liked Kingdom Hearts II Final Mix +, Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days and Final Fantasy VII Advent Children. Of those, I played a ton of Kingdom Hearts II Final Mix +.

—— Oh yeah, Kingdom Hearts II Final Mix + is the powered-up version of that game. We can really tell that you like it. (laughs) Those who know, know, but you played MONOTONE (a cell phone game for the i-mode service) as well, right?

Nomura Really? (laughs)

TAKUMI Yes. (laughs)

—— By the time REYNATIS was deep in development, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth had come out, but surely...?

TAKUMI Of course I found time to play it.

Moving to details about how the NTWEWY development team was very much involved in the collaboration
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— What is the level of the content for this collaboration with NTWEWY, exactly?

TAKUMI At the beginning, I wanted to have the NTWEWY logo appear on a sign or something or have the characters have costumes [from NTWEWY], at the very least.

However, when I spoke to the NTWEWY team they said, "If you're going to do it, you should go all the way." So, in the end, there is a completely new scenario, as well as [playable] stages in this collaboration, so it's very ample.

—— Did you have any requests regarding the content, Mr. Nomura?

Nomura I wanted to respect the wishes of the various members of the team, so I basically left everything up to them and TAKUMI. Of course, the underlying expectation was that things would be kept within reason… So, all I said was to adjust the color tone of NTWEWY to match the color tone of REYNATIS.

—— That's right; NTWEWY has a distinct design that is 2D and comic-like. It must have been necessary to do some trial and error to get that right with the design of REYNATIS.

TAKUMI At first, we really struggled with how to make it fit. But, just as in the movie Spider-man: Into the Spider-Verse, there are works that purposefully do not try to match the visuals of the characters from different world settings, and I had the impression that viewers accept that well.

We didn't try to force the NTWEWY designs to fit in with REYNATIS and just adjusted the color tone, so the character graphics are very NTWEWY-like.

Nomura In contrast to the somewhat moody color tone of the REYNATIS backgrounds, the lines of the NTWEWY characters are stark. I thought that if we tried to adjust that aspect to those moody backgrounds, the characters' outlines would stand out in a bad way, so I thought it would be okay to just adjust the color tone [of those lines].

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/50945e914d63a6018c727fd36466d3ab2af621af.jpg

TAKUMI Outside of the characters, we used the Noise lines and effects [from NTWEWY], so we were able to blend the atmosphere of REYNATIS and NTWEWY without it feeling strange.

—— I heard that for the collaboration's story, NTWEWY's Scenario Writer Akiko Ishibashi worked on it.

TAKUMI I came up with the plot and presented it and, after that, Ms. Ishibashi brushed it up to make it fit with NTWEWY.

—— So you wrote the plot, TAKUMI?

TAKUMI There was no one else who knew the characters and world setting of REYNATIS in addition to possessing the knowledge of NTWEWY more than me, so I thought it would be quickest if I came up with the plot.

—— What other interactions did you have with the NTWEWY team?

TAKUMI I spoke remotely with NTWEWY's Producer, Tomohiko Hirano, and the Director, Tatsuya Kando. We had some short interactions where they checked over what we were making.

—— So, the main staff of NTWEWY are all very involved with this collaboration. What does this collaboration have to do with the main story of REYNATIS?

TAKUMI It is a subquest that stems off of the main story of REYNATIS. It's made so that even people who aren't familiar with NTWEWY will be able to enjoy it.

—— Rindo and Shoka appear in the trailer, but aside from them, do other [NTWEWY] characters appear?

TAKUMI As an enemy, ●●●● also appears. Particularly, for the fight with ●●●●, we made a special stage that completely recreates the fight in NTWEWY. Also, we plan to have ●●●● make an appearance, as well.

Nomura You should really keep stuff like that under wraps for now.

TAKUMI Ah, you're right.

Nomura Please look forward to it!

[previewyoutube=oKABHYylwlE;full][/previewyoutube]

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/1cfad7c9fcd7f42989f0f7042dfbed204cdfce47.gif

—— Well, now everyone's curious. (laughs) The voice actress for both the main character of REYNATIS, Sari, and Shoka from TWEWY, is Akari Kito. I felt like there are other voice actors from Mr. Nomura's works that appear in REYNATIS. Was this casting intentional?

TAKUMI It was…intentional.

Nomura You go, man. (laughs)

TAKUMI For example, there is an enemy researcher [in REYNATIS] named Shinzaburo Kiyokawa. Well, when I say "researcher," I mean mad scientist. And when I thought of mad scientists, I thought of Shigeru Chiba (he also played the mad scientist Dr. Hojo in Final Fantasy VII), so we offered the role to him.

—— With this much respect for Square Enix's works, or rather, Mr. Nomura's, I would think that the player might end up comparing REYNATIS to those games. Did you feel any pressure that the players might compare them?

TAKUMI I didn't feel pressure. To begin with, the budget gap between a Square Enix game and a FURYU Corporation game is large. As a FURYU Corporation game, it was important to make the message of the game and its concept be the core, so in order for players to feel those areas the most, we put most of our budget there.

I've worked hard to create a game that conveys the message I want to express to users so that they think, "This game was made for me" to feel close to the game. Focusing on bringing out a message and relatability to make it different from anything else is something that I think people can enjoy.

The theme of REYNATIS is for those who feel the difficulty of living under peer pressure coming together, and if that theme is able to be properly conveyed, I would be pleased if this game has a palpable appeal unlike any other game out there.

What a director should be, according to TAKUMI and Mr. Nomura
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— Now, I'd like to hear your thoughts as [game] creators. First, TAKUMI, can you tell us how you became a game creator?

TAKUMI My mother is a designer and [she taught me] about art and design from when I was small. So, at first, I wanted to be a designer, but, starting with Kingdom Hearts, I encountered many different games and, since I enjoyed creating things, I thought, "I want to make games, particularly using my own original ideas," and this feeling grew stronger. At first, it was a very simple idea where I thought, "I can draw, so if I can do [game] planning and learn how to program, I can make my own original games."

—— Oh, so you can draw as well! That's just like Mr. Nomura…

Nomura I can't program, though. (laughs) I've only fooled around in BASIC.

—— Would you say that being able to program is representative of today's game creators?

TAKUMI I actually majored in programming in graduate school, but I put the brakes on myself because I thought, "Aw man, this isn't fun. Programming just isn't for me. I can't do this." However, I did have the basic skill set [for programming] down as well as the knowledge and thought process, so with my ability to draw and create design documents, I thought, "I just might be able to become the best [game] planner out there." (laughs) And then I was able to join FURYU Corporation.

—— Why did you choose FURYU Corporation out of all the game developers out there?

TAKUMI One of the appealing points of FURYU Corporation was that, even if you're young, the company has a culture of allowing you to make your own original games if you have the will and the ability. I think that at other companies, you would need to be a certain age or have paid your dues before being allowed to make a game. Especially now, games can take several years to a decade to make, so I don't even know how one would go about paying their dues in that situation. For those reasons, I went with FURYU Corporation.

—— I see. But didn't you think that you would want to join Square Enix?

TAKUMI I love Square Enix, and particularly Mr. Nomura's works, but that doesn't mean that I want to make Kingdom Hearts. I feel that, in order to become a creator like Mr. Nomura, I must come up with my own, original ideas.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/56ee544fa5c7629b0452de0c8eb69fad0d60ddc0.jpg
—— So your creative desires won out. You studied drawing, but you didn't think to do character design like Mr. Nomura?

TAKUMI I can't draw the kinds of appealing things that Mr. Nomura can, so I never thought about becoming a character designer.

Nomura There are plenty of people who are good at drawing, but there are only a handful of those who can actually design characters. I think it's a difficult genre [to excel in]. Even now, I think it's difficult to design characters myself.

TAKUMI You were originally a pixel artist, right?

Nomura Correct. And from that work, I eventually wound up being allowed to direct games.

—— That's certainly unique. Did you always want to be a director?

Nomura Not at all. To begin with, I didn't even want to be a character designer. I simply enjoyed the mere act of participating in game development. I did have plenty of opportunities to present game plans though.

Within that, I started to enjoy coming up with game plans. So, while continuing my main work of illustration, I continued to present game plans, and I then happened upon the fateful opportunity that was Kingdom Hearts.

—— Speaking of Kingdom Hearts, there's a famous episode where a conversation took place in an elevator in the Arc Tower in Meguro (※1) between people from Square Enix and a top person from Walt Disney Japan, right?

Nomura I wasn't in that elevator myself, so I don't know exactly what was said, but, by chance, I happened to be where Mr. Sakaguchi (※2) and Mr. Hashimoto (※3) said that Square Enix was going to make a Disney game, and I raised my hand to volunteer to work on it.

Looking back at it, I can't even remember why I was in the same place with Mr. Sakaguchi and Mr. Hashimoto when they were talking about this. (laughs)
[olist]※1: The building that Square (currently Square Enix) used to occupy.
※2: Shinji Hashimoto. Former brand manager of the Final Fantasy series. Current senior advisor for Sony Music Entertainment.
※3: Hironobu Sakaguchi. Father of the Final Fantasy series. Current CEO of Mistwalker Corporation.[/olist]—— So, it was just a series of coincidences. But, the reason you raised your hand was because you had an idea for a game you wanted to make, right?

Nomura At the time, when I was working on Final Fantasy VII, Super Mario 64 was released. I was deeply impressed by the game and how you could move around freely in 3D space. Thanks to that, I vaguely had an idea that I wanted to make an action game where you could move around freely. I had told my junior in the company about that and they said, "In that case, it can't be a new IP. It needs to be a worldwide/globally known IP precisely like Disney!" I thought, "I see…"

—— [Being able to work] on a globally known IP is easy to say… But, from there, you spoke to Mr. Sakaguchi and Mr. Hashimoto, right?

Nomura Exactly. I thought, "This is the connection I was waiting for!"

TAKUMI What an amazing story. (laughs)

—— Luck and timing are certainly important.

Nomura After that, I figured the only game I would be the director on was Kingdom Hearts, but before I knew it, I was working as the director for various titles. Still, my main job was as an illustrator.

—— With all these titles under your belt, what is something that you always keep in mind as a director?

Nomura A director cannot make a game alone. They are making the game with the rest of the development team, so they must never forget that these other people are working on the game with them. That is something I haven't changed my stance on since Kingdom Hearts.

A great amount of time must be spent on development, and there are things that the director must not budge on, and in those instances, you have to remember that you're having the staff go along with your whims and not forget your feelings of gratitude to them for that.

Other than that, I want the other staff members to have fun working on the game. If it becomes a project important to each member, that leads to them being motivated to work on it.

TAKUMI From that point of view, which title would you say has left the biggest impression on you?

Nomura Naturally, Kingdom Hearts. It was my first time as director and it was difficult figuring out how to proceed. Staff members would have friction or differing opinions and I had to be the one to mediate…

—— You mediate yourself?!

Nomura Surprisingly, I'm the empathetic type. (laughs)

—— Easily approachable and empathetic! It's important to have a good vibe within the team, isn't it?

Nomura I'm not sure if I'd call it a vibe, but it's important to allow what the staff participating in the project want to do and respect their wishes as much as possible. When I was just another staff member myself, I remember there were things that I wanted to do that I would propose, and I was happy when they would use my ideas and I want [my teams] to experience the same thing.

—— How about you, TAKUMI? What do you keep in mind/focus on as a director?

TAKUMI I also think it's important to have my team enjoy what they're doing. If they're enjoying what they are doing, they will be more motivated and there are many cases where the results are even better than what you were looking for.

Of course, though they are enjoying themselves and have freedom, it is important to course correct at times, as well. I think the role of the director is to create an environment where [the staff] can enjoy what they are doing with a positive attitude.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/056439d9346c7c4ccf4565a56a1dc1e9f2bca67a.jpg

The many game plans sleeping within Mr. Nomura's PC- Even "that game"!
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— TAKUMI, using this opportunity, is there anything you would like to ask Mr. Nomura?

TAKUMI Of course! When you think about creating a new IP, where do you start?

Nomura I think about the world setting, then I come up with a synopsis and the characters, and I keep those ideas to myself. When I'm asked by the game producer about plans for a game, I present the plans that I have been keeping to myself if it fits the situation. Then, we adjust [so it fits with what's needed].

TAKUMI That's a unique way of doing things.

Nomura When the producer comes to me, I gather my ideas after asking what hardware it will be for, whether it will be developed internally or externally, and what genre it should be.

—— Do elements like the hardware or development environment affect the content of the game?

Nomura Depending on the hardware, the play experience is different, and the scale of the development changes what kinds of world settings can be done, so it has a significant impact on the plans.

—— Do you keep your ideas as actual documentation?

Nomura In order to easily share my image of the project to others, first I find images or photos on the internet and, using those as references, I create a fake title screen. After that, I write up a brief synopsis.

—— So, even at the "idea" level, you write up a synopsis.

Nomura I think that unless you can get the producer excited when you are explaining the project, it's no good, so I make sure to write up a synopsis so that I don't forget the contents myself. Then, I throw all that into a folder and that's that.

TAKUMI "That's that"?

Nomura Yes. Then, when there's talk of making a new game, I go into the folders and adjust a little and format it [appropriately]. For ideas that I don't use, those get put back into the folder to get brushed up at a later date. This process is constantly repeated. Those brushed-up game plans then get put into a folder called "NEW."

TAKUMI Do you have a big stock of these game ideas?

Nomura It's getting smaller and smaller. However, there is a folder with a ton of game plans that haven't been used. There're entire scenarios in there, too.

TAKUMI I'd love to see that folder...

Nomura That folder has different sub-folders, and it's practically a labyrinth at this point, so even I don't know if some of those ideas will ever see the light of day.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/5e8ec5b37138ae2e67f97f5e703a2ad2531ff52d.jpg

—— Please be sure to back up the data in that folder! How about you, TAKUMI? How do you go about making your ideas for game plans?

TAKUMI I work backward by first having an idea for a scene that I want to portray. Then, in order to make that scene, I come up with the necessary world, the setting, and the characters. REYNATIS was also created in this way.

—— Do you have a stock of game plans yourself, TAKUMI?

TAKUMI I do have a few game plans in stock. At FURYU Corporation, the focal point, scope, and time period for game development are all set, and compared to other companies, the development period is basically set at about 3 years, which is on the short side. So, for my game plans, I always keep in mind what is trending at the time to add that to the game to make it appealing.

—— Is there something that you do to keep yourself aware of current trends?

TAKUMI FURYU Corporation also has a photo booth machine business, so I make it a point to periodically check what's trending amongst young people and their slang and the like through the staff in that division.

The pair want the collaboration to spark interest in both REYNATIS and TWEWY!
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— The fact that you both have a stock of game ideas is something that we can all really look forward to, but please tell us what your goals are as creators from here on out.

TAKUMI REYNATIS has been set up on a very large foundation, and I still have plenty of ideas for it, so I would be really happy to expand the world of this game into a franchise.

Nomura In my case, first and foremost, I want to stay healthy.

—— (Laugh) Health… Yes, that is very important.

Nomura And, including all the titles that have been announced, there are still titles that I need to make, so I'd like to keep plugging away at those. I only recently learned this, but apparently, abroad, it's being said that I have an illness.

—— Huh?

Nomura I have no clue where that rumor started, but I'm totally healthy.

—— That rumor should disappear after this interview. How did you feel about this conversation with TAKUMI?

Nomura Looking at the current space for console games, TAKUMI is a very young director and producer. The result of his desire to create what he wanted is this game: REYNATIS. This isn't really the type of game you see the likes of recently, so I really hope the players give the game a chance and spread the word.

And with REYNATIS as a starting gun, I hope that other young creators will follow and a new trend will be born in this industry. I'd like TAKUMI to break open the way [for others]. I won't allow failure, because that would portend something really awful.

—— You certainly raised the bar for him at the end there. (laughs)

Nomura I never thought that I would see the NTWEWY characters in action again. I think that the characters who appear in this collaboration, Rindo and Shoka, are very well-realized, so I'm very grateful that new life was breathed into them. I would like fans of NTWEWY to see how these characters come out here and, for those who aren't familiar with NTWEWY, I hope that [this collaboration] encourages them to give it a try.

In the series, there are only two games: TWEWY and NTWEWY, so I think it's an easy series to get into. I hope that you enjoy both those games, as well as this collaboration with REYNATIS.

—— And how about closing things out, TAKUMI?

TAKUMI We had this opportunity to do a collaboration event between REYNATIS and NTWEWY. There are other characters and bosses in the trailer, as well as an original story and various other elements that players will enjoy in this collaboration. REYNATIS is only one game, so I think it's easy to get into. (laughs) Anyone can get started, and this is the only chance you'll get to start from the first game. Should the series continue from here, it will be more difficult to start, so I would love for you to give this game a try.

Nomura If you start from the first game, then you can call yourself an OG.

TAKUMI Taking a peek at social media, I get the impression that people have been turned onto the TWEWY series from REYNATIS. I would be happy if this collaboration kicked off interest in the TWEWY series. It would also be great if it led to a sequel to NTWEWY. Everyone out there, please give this collaboration between REYNATIS and NTWEWY a chance!

notes.title: Shibuya Guide
notes.content:
REYNATIS features the painstakingly-recreated streets of Shibuya, Tokyo, complete with over 100 authentic shops and restaurants. Whether you've visited Shibuya many times, or are planning a future trip, we've got the scoop on everything you'll need to know about the iconic locations featured in the game.

Plus, REYNATIS Creative Producer TAKUMI has shared his insights on why he selected Shibuya as the location for REYNATIS, behind-the-scenes of the development process, what area screams “Shibuya,” and more!

[previewyoutube=upW0henlFik;full][/previewyoutube]
Shibuya and REYNATIS go hand in hand. When discussing the reason for choosing Shibuya as REYNATIS' location, TAKUMI emphasizes the importance of players being able to relate to the themes he wanted to explore.

“If you do something different from others, are unconventional, or wear expressive clothing, you get flack,” TAKUMI says. As a result, “that wonderful individuality gets hidden… and you end up with no uniqueness.”

In contrast to this mentality, TAKUMI sought to explore themes around accepting others, expressing individuality, and celebrating uniqueness in REYNATIS. In order for players to resonate with these themes, TAKUMI felt it was necessary to have the game's setting be something that was an extension of the real world.

“From there… I decided to choose a place in Japan that would be comparatively well-known, yet also underground, with back alleyways that could be explored.”

“In the end, I chose Shibuya.”

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/5d6d515cdb25f9677c46cb5f8ea084bd90bf629a.jpg

Streets Constantly Under Change
Did you know that the FURYU Corporation offices are in Shibuya? Because of that, TAKUMI goes to Shibuya nearly every day. “I also have many memories of shopping or hanging out in Shibuya,” he says. “Because of that, each of my memories there are special.”

But things are constantly changing, which means new shops are popping up all the time. “Just walking around Shibuya, there might be a building that wasn't there the week before, or vice versa,” he recalls. “It was nerve-wracking. Due to that, my impressions of Shibuya were always changing.”

During the development of REYNATIS, TAKUMI and the development team were paying particularly close attention to the streets of Shibuya in order to authentically replicate them in the game. TAKUMI says that he has the most fond memories of Shibuya from this time.

“I would say my special memories of Shibuya are particularly strong during the time when REYNATIS was under development. In order to recreate Shibuya in the game, we would walk around taking pictures to get a feel for the area's atmosphere/vibe,” he says.

Each of the areas of Shibuya certainly have their own vibe. Let's take a look at a few up close and see what TAKUMI has to say about them!

Location 1: Dogenzaka
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/7db862884d9fa375c92c1c22661fb93d69297c4d.jpg
This street is a hub for shopping, food, and Shibuya nightlife. There, you'll find everything from name-brand stores and chain restaurants to Japanese izakaya (a casual Japanese eatery that serves alcohol and food) and clubs.

TAKUMI's Comment:
Dogenzaka is honestly kind of a "deep cut" area, and gives off a dangerous vibe. (laughs)
I remember going there to take pictures and thinking about what a dangerous place it was.

Location 2: Shibuya Center Gai
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/a07801cd4573a975bde05d23161a01e20fe0e7ac.jpgThis central hub for youth culture is known for the latest fashion and music trends. And when night falls, immerse yourself in Shibuya's nightlife entertainment!

TAKUMI's Comment:
Every time I went here, the shops and buildings had changed. This area was always a nuisance [in terms of how to portray it in-game]. We tried as hard as we could to replicate the shops that had been there for a long time, as well as other places that stood out.

Location 3: Spain Hill
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/59691175d9bc391223f64b9deec56e03845255d4.jpg
This narrow street is packed with interesting shops. The Ningen Kankei café has been around since 1979 and is known for its excellent scones!

TAKUMI's Comment:
This is the narrowest area in the game. However, we have faithfully reproduced the shops that line either side, so there might be a few you know. Maybe [the ramen shop] Ichiran? Personally, I like Ichiran, and I used to go there often, so I made sure that it was reproduced in the game.

Location 4: Shibuya Scramble Crossing
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/45d19c6204a4280ea85f8bde6f1b1077623d761d.jpg
This iconic crosswalk is located right outside Shibuya Station and is lined with many iconic signs and advertisements. At the entrance to Shibuya station, you will find the famous Hachiko statue, which has been transformed into a crow in the world of REYNATIS.

TAKUMI's Comment:
This is a symbol of Shibuya, so it was the first area that we created. Even at night, this place has a lot of people and it's really earned its name as the world's busiest intersection. Watching people manage to cross without bumping into one another is strange and charming. There are people of all ages and races crossing all going to different locations from there. It's fun to imagine [where they might all be going].

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/2ae73a083e4d8fdf4a15db0e6cd886fbbf80d068.jpg

However, during the COVID-19 pandemic when the emergency declarations were made, even it was unbelievably empty. That's exactly how it is in REYNATIS. Because there are dangerous wizards, the area is under a state of emergency.

The Area that Just Screams 'Shibuya'
When it comes to locations in the game, TAKUMI says his favorite is the section from Shibuya Scramble Crossing to the area around the Shibuya 109 building. “I guess you could say it's the place that leaves the strongest impression of Shibuya. I'll bet it's also a famous symbol of Shibuya in Japanese tourist guides.”

“Here's a little behind the scenes episode,” he relates. “Originally, we had intended for the Shibuya Scramble Crossing and the area in front of the 109 building to be implemented as separate areas. The reason for this is that there are many signs and buildings, so we thought we had to be careful of memory limitations in order to have a maximum of three characters fight there smoothly."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/a0e221a8fedc0f9e86785186114f8e73cb5a935b.jpg

“However, you can see Shibuya 109 from the Scramble Crossing, and as you get closer to it, that area just screams 'Shibuya,' so we had to have it in the game, and I asked the dev team to somehow make those areas connected. I really want players to experience [that feeling].”

As the first location in Shibuya worked on in the game, TAKUMI describes this section between Shibuya Scramble Crossing and the Shibuya 109 building as REYNATIS' place of origin.” And, thanks to the hard work the devs put into the game, the two areas are connected, allowing players to see and experience the exact moment TAKUMI describes.

Experience the Shibuya of REYNATIS
Even if you haven't visited Shibuya in real life, REYNATIS will give you the chance to experience the bustling streets of Tokyo for yourself.

“I would love players to explore the Shibuya in REYNATIS then compare it with the real-life Shibuya,” TAKUMI says. “Each area was recreated with a high degree of fidelity, so it could be like a pilgrimage.”

notes.title: REYNATIS x NEO: The World Ends With You Interview
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/032617e7c5ae3c83df401452f1e8de4fa529097c.jpg

REYNATIS Creative Producer TAKUMI and three key members of the NEO: The World Ends With You development team, Creative Producer and Character Designer Tetsuya Nomura, Producer Tomohiko Hirano, and the Series Director Tatsuya Kando discuss the upcoming NEO: The World Ends With You collaboration with REYNATIS, such as what drives game creators, Tetsuya Nomura's advice for young creators, and more.

* This article was originally published on the NIS America website. You can find the original content at the following link: REYNATIS x NEO: The World Ends With You Interview.

With both games sharing a modern-day Shibuya setting with fantasy elements, the REYNATIS x NEO: The World Ends With You collaboration is a match made in heaven. And it all began with the passion of REYNATIS' Creative Producer TAKUMI and his admiration for Tetsuya Nomura, the game creator involved in the Kingdom Hearts series, along with a multitude of other projects.

For this interview, Denfamicogamer sought to find out what drew TAKUMI to Tetusya Nomura's works and NEO: The World Ends With You, resulting in the following roundtable discussion about how the collaboration came about.

Please enjoy the translated version below!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/e90404ed6a5d24593dfd08488e5a7064028a9dc2.png

A young creator's passion that transcended company boundaries
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— I think it's rare for a collaboration to overcome the barrier of two different companies both working in the console games market. To start us off, how were you first told about this collaboration, Mr. Nomura?

Tetsuya Nomura (hereafter Nomura) Hirano here told me that “Someone wants to discuss doing a collaboration,” and I took a look at the planning documents. I thought, “Wow. They sure going for it.” (laughs)

All (laughs)

Nomura TAKUMI's overflowing enthusiasm was evident from the very detailed planning documents.

Being confronted with his affection towards The World Ends With You made me want to participate in the collaboration and want it to succeed. So, I told Hirano, “Do what you can to help him out.”

Isobe Takumi (hereafter TAKUMI) It's an honor to hear you say that.

REYNATIS is a game that's set in Shibuya, but even though various shops and landmarks appear [in the game] under their real names, when I think of Shibuya, I just think of the one in The World Ends With You. I thought, “Even if it doesn't work out, I should still offer my proposal,” and that's what kicked this off.

—— The companies making REYNATIS and NEO: The World Ends With You are different, so how were you able to reach out to them with your proposal? Did you have some connection to someone who was on theThe World Ends With You team?

TAKUMI No, I didn't have any connections, so I didn't have an “in” to propose the collaboration.

I talked to [FURYU Corporation's] sales staff and, by chance, they had a connection to Square Enix's marketing person, who then introduced me to Mr. Hirano.

Tomohiko Hirano (hereafter Hirano) When I first heard about it, I really felt TAKUMI's passion and enthusiasm. Then, I was really surprised when I saw the planning documents.

—— Wow, really? When you first spoke to Mr. Hirano, did you have some kind of plan in mind to get him on board to make this collaboration a reality?

TAKUMI At that point, I just took the planning document with all the information I could include in it and put everything out in the open. It wasn't anything businesslike. It really was just me presenting it like, “I really like The World Ends With You!”

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/87995b30ee1bb75fd31b575fe3b5a81aa638bb14.jpg

Hirano I can say this now, but during that meeting, I said, “If you want to do a collaboration that involves Shibuya, there are other more famous works [than The World Ends With You], so you don't need to sugarcoat anything.”

But TAKUMI said forcefully, “I want to do a collaboration with The World Ends With You!” That made me think, “He must really be a fan of ours…” (laughs)

TAKUMI Precisely. I am a fan. (laughs)

Since Kingdom Hearts, I've played practically all of your titles. I encountered your games in my formative years, so I was greatly influenced by them.

—— So that's how this collaboration came to be. Naturally, you must have been really fired up then, right, TAKUMI?

TAKUMI I was. Abundantly so. So much so that people said I was only this fired up when working on the NEO: The World Ends With You collaboration.

Also, I didn't just want this collaboration to include simple elements. I wanted to have a deeply involved collaboration that the fans would be satisfied with, so I had the initial development schedule lengthened.

From not wanting to do a “haphazard collaboration” to one where both works are deeply intertwined
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— So, this began with TAKUMI's enthusiasm. What would you say is the main draw for this REYNATIS and NEO: The World Ends With You collaboration?

TAKUMI First and foremost, I want people to pay attention to the story. I think seeing how the characters of REYNATIS and NEO: The World Ends With You become involved with one another is particularly noteworthy.

Tatsuya Kando (hereunder Kando) The story in this collaboration runs parallel to the events of NEO: The World Ends With You, and we decided to set it at the beginning of the game, shortly after when Rindo first gets involved with the Wicked Twisters.

If I say too much it would spoil it, so I'll keep the details to a minimum, but Rindo and Shoka are antagonistic to one another, and they are transported to another world where they must work together to return to their world. I thought it was an interesting story.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/1806ff3a3d147fbbbffdef2e142efd5dc273cbcf.jpg

—— For this collaboration, I have the impression that characters don't just make cameos but rather are deeply intertwined with one another. I'm surprised this was approved.

Hirano Seriously speaking, this collaboration is “anything [is ok] within the confines of the contract,” so we [Square Enix] didn't have any hesitation about going with the proposal.

In regards to the nuts and bolts of the collaboration, we received the proposal from TAKUMI, and showed it to both Mr. Nomura and Mr. Kando. We proceeded once we had their approval.

—— How was the content itself decided?

TAKUMI First, I compiled everything that I wanted to do. Then those plans were revised in discussions with Mr. Hirano and Mr. Kando.

Hirano We wanted to make the most of this collaboration, so we made sure to make requests of our own. We worked together with TAKUMI to finalize everything.

Kando Thankfully, we believe that The World Ends With You is a series enthusiastically supported by fans, so we knew a haphazard collaboration wouldn't do. We knew it had to be content we could confidently offer to fans.

Therefore, we made sure that Shoka and the others appeared appropriately in REYNATIS by making sure our own ideas were conveyed. That's how we decided on the content.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/3335e7896d4fdfbf86a8602ca014189e084185f2.jpg

—— Was there anything that you had to particularly watch out for from the perspective of [employees on behalf of] Square Enix?

Kando We simply combined REYNATIS and NEO: The World Ends With You, but the worlds [of the games] don't really fit well together, so we had to think about how we could create a situation where neither would overpower what was good about the other.

In the end, we wound up making a “world between the worlds,” which is where this collaboration plays out.

—— So, that's when NEO: The World Ends With You's scenario writer Mr. Ishibashi came to be the scenario writer for this [collaboration], right?

Kando That's correct. TAKUMI had drawn up the foundation for the project, so myself, Mr. Itō the director, and Mr. Ishibashi put the content together.

From there, we fixed the plot to make it adhere to the “rules” of NEO: The World Ends With You, and then had Mr. Ishibashi write the text.

Hirano Incidentally, we were the ones who requested that the BGM be taken straight from NEO: The World Ends With You.

Kando That's right; Mr. Itō had strong feelings about when and where the BGM should be used.

TAKUMI Personally, I was really surprised at just how much we could do in this collaboration. So, as a fan of The World Ends With You, I decided to act as the representative for The World Ends With You fans and was constantly thinking, “What would the fans enjoy?”

As we proceeded, I thought about things like, “I wonder if we could have that one character from NEO: The World Ends With You speak with this character from REYANTIS.”

From sharing characters to advice, the NEO: The World Ends With You team gave their full support.
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— It's like the developers of both games came together as one for this collaboration. But TAKUMI, when you made the proposal, did you ever think in your wildest dreams that you would be able to make Rindo and Shoka from NEO: The World Ends With You?

TAKUMI Not at all. I was so happy.

I played The World Ends With You series when it first came out on the Nintendo DS, so as the producer of REYNATIS and as a fan of The World Ends With You, I really wanted to preserve the appeal of each and every character.

To that end, I thought carefully and continuously about how to effectively involve them in REYNATIS.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/3c4511c1cc822abec538352a1159c45362c557a5.jpg

—— This is a simple question from me, but the graphical assets for Rindo and Shoka were done by FURYU Corporation, right?

TAKUMI No, we basically received all of that data [from Square Enix].

—— Wow, really?!

TAKUMI However, we couldn't use them as-is in the game, so we had to adjust things so that they would work in REYNATIS.

Hirano Basically, we gave them everything we could. I bet TAKUMI was puzzled, wondering, “Why are they offering all this data?” (laughs)

Fortunately, both games run on Unity, so the work [to get the assets adjusted for REYNATIS] was relatively speedy.

TAKUMI I updated them frequently about the progress. I went drinking with Mr. Hirano often, so I had plenty of chances to explain the progress and get advice, which allowed me to proceed with the project without too much worry.

Hirano That's right. When he would show me the progress, I would say things like, “This part isn't really The World Ends With You-like,” so once he fixed it, I would send it around internally for approval.

Nomura Mr. Hirano, they're gonna headhunt you.

All (laughs)

—— By the way, what, to you, is “The World Ends With You-like?”

TAKUMI For me, the big appeal of Mr. Nomura's works is that they are set in the real world, with fantasy elements.

I think The World Ends With You is the title that best exemplifies that, so that's what I consider “The World Ends With You-like.”

—— What did you think at Square Enix once you saw the finished collaboration?

Kando The World Ends With You is unique for its thickly drawn 2D black lines, so we thought, “How do we replicate that look with polygons?” Keeping that in mind is how we got NEO: The World Ends With You.

We were a little uncertain about how blending that unique touch with REYNATIS' more realistic style would turn out.

However, when we saw the finished product we thought, “Hey, that doesn't look unnatural at all.” The enemies–Noise–also retained that touch in battle, so we had no objections from our side about the finished product.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/28fb8351fd267e5b1d5a09c780eccd36bafcb9c9.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/b3d66ec0367581b094bcde4dd7e33c1601658372.jpg

—— Mr. Nomura, was there anything that stood out to you?

Nomura In terms of the graphics, the deepness/saturation of the colors stood out to me, so I mentioned that. Other than that, I thought, “If we're really going all out with this, it should be voiced.”

Hirano When we were first approached about the collaboration, REYNATIS itself was already pretty far along in development.

The story for this collaboration is implemented as a kind of substory, but I heard that there wouldn't be enough time in the schedule to include additional voice acting. I'm sure TAKUMI wishes we could have done even more than we did…

Takumi We'll do it in REYNATIS 2.

Kando That was quick!

All (laughs)

REYNATIS — a game created from TAKUMI's interpretation of Shibuya
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— Mr. Hirano and Mr. Kando, could you tell us your first impressions of REYNATIS?

Kando …"He's sure going for it."

Hirano That's what I just said! (laughs)

Kando I think there are several games out there that use Shibuya as a setting, each with their own interpretation of Shibuya. Even though TAKUMI respects The World Ends With You, his personal interpretation of Shibuya is what makes REYNATIS. My first impression was that if we could combine his work with our own, it would be very interesting.

Nomura Don't you think it's human nature to want someone to succeed in their passion when they present it to you in such a straightforward and honest manner? If there was some kind of ulterior motive, I don't think he would have been so upfront with how he approached us.

—— So, you think such honesty is rare?

Hirano Yeah, we don't even hear about something like that at our own company.

Nomura I thought TAKUMI's straightforwardness and humility were great.

—— I see. The look of a town can change quite a lot in a five to 10 year timeframe, so I think there are differences between the Shibuya of NEO: The World Ends With You and REYNATIS. When you were reviewing the project, did you feel anything in particular about this [aspect]?

Hirano It's not just the look of Shibuya between NEO: The World Ends With You and REYNATIS, but the impression of the town itself. The setting of Shibuya in NEO: The World Ends With You is during the day, whereas I would say it's nighttime for REYNATIS. Furthermore, I would say another big point of difference between the two is that NEO: The World Ends With You is more of an anime-style, while REYNATIS is going for something more photorealistic.

—— The difference between night and day, I see. TAKUMI, did you intend to portray Shibuya at night?

Takumi The concept for the wizards in REYNATIS is that they are oppressed and must live in the shadows, not allowing their identities to be known by normal people. Since this was the setup, it made sense for wizards to have to move around at night.

—— In the Shibuya of both REYNATIS and NEO: The World Ends With You, real-world shops make an appearance. I'm sure getting the adequeite permissions to do that was difficult. Did you ask Square Enix for some pointers on how to go about that, TAKUMI?

Takumi I did ask Mr. Hirano about that at the beginning.

Hirano However, there are more real-world shops in REYNATIS than there are in NEO: The World Ends With You, so you can chalk that up to TAKUMI's hard work.

Takumi Well, the actual buildings and number of shops in Shibuya at the time were completely different, so it's not possible to do a total comparison, but I appreciate the praise. Still, everyone on the development team helped out a lot, so I would give them the lion's share of the credit for their hard work.

Hirano I'm sure getting permission from that many shops was really difficult.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/c0adf7cc7e44063e50f010d47764c2497b3689eb.jpg

The driving force behind game development: The desire to make others happy
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— Continuing the conversation, I'd like to ask you a personal question, TAKUMI. What would you say your motivation is for creating games?

Takumi Ever since I was small, I always felt like I could make my own toys if I wasn't able to buy any. I would have my friends check out the things I had made and enjoyed watching them play with them. Looking back at that now, I strongly feel that the joy in that is my motivation.

—— So, what would you say is at the core of your creative drive?

Takumi I've always felt that there are many people who want to express themselves but aren't able to do so. "The nail that sticks up gets hammered down," as they say. [Editor's note: This is common Japanese proverb.]

That's a theme and concept for REYNATIS, but [the thought that], "Hey everyone, it's alright to express your individuality, and you can go as wild as you'd like with it," was also at the heart [of it]. Other than that, I have to say that I like things with a dark atmosphere. I guess I have a longing to be more like a light character, hence my appearance.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/dc3fc72a8e73f2aa4e94abf8f0aa69a688508182.jpg

All (laughs)

—— By the way, when you first met Mr. Nomura, did you have the same pink hair as you do now?

Takumi I think I did…

—— In that case, were you surprised by that, Mr. Nomura?

Nomura Mr. Kazushige Nojima, who is the Scenario Writer for REYNATIS, wrote on X (formerly Twitter), "Every time I meet him, his hair is a different color," so I wasn't surprised.

Kando That's true! I feel like every time we had a remote meeting, his hair was a different color. (laughs)

—— It seems that Mr. Isobe's hair proclivities were a well-known entity even then. This next question is for Mr. Nomura: What is your motivation for making games?

Nomura Seriously speaking, since I was young I've had many ideas building up for things I've wanted to create. But no matter how hard you try, games take years to come together, right? So that means you just end up with a bunch of ideas. Right now, I'm trying to bring as many of those to fruition as I can.

And, the core of what keeps me involved in creative works is the desire to "make others happy."

When I was in school, I used to draw manga in class and have my friends read it. On my days off, I would sketch out plans for table-top games on paper and take them to school with me. I loved when others enjoyed something that I had made.

No lies in creative works with modern-day settings
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— Since we have this opportunity, I'd like to ask about "input" in regards to game development. TAKUMI, what kind of things do you take note of?

Takumi I don't really think, "I should absorb this!" Rather, if I come across something that makes me feel "I can use this," in my daily life, I write that down, so I've built up a stock of things.

Nomura I watch a lot of movies. I actually went and saw one today.

—— What did you watch?

Nomura Mission Impossible: Ghost Protocol.

—— What kinds of genres do you usually watch?

Nomura A variety. My favorite [genre] is horror. I'm subscribed to pretty much every subscription service out there, and I watch a lot of horror on all of them.

Takumi Interesting. What's your favorite?

Nomura I've been watching them for such a long time, I don't remember all of the names. When I was sorting my collection at home, I found out that I had three copies of the same movie. (laughs) Of what I do remember, I guess Sinister. Basically, I like POV fake documentaries.

Takumi Oh, that's cool!

Nomura Recently, I also watched Marui Video.

—— Why do you like fake documentaries?

Nomura Many of the games that I make are set in the modern day, and this is related to that, but I really don't like lies in creative works.

A truely scary horror movie doesn't exist. As you watch, you end up thinking, "this is just fiction," so there's nothing really scary.

So, that feeling of reality in a fake documentary provides that creepy feeling I'm after. Recently, I thought Incantation and The Medium were really good.

Takumi This is a Japanese TV show, but do you know Amasso no Ganbare Okusama!? It seems like a variety show at first blush, but actually, something pretty shocking happens… I thought I was just watching a variety TV show, so I was really surprised. It was super interesting.

Nomura Huh. I guess I know the twist now.

To keep making games, "prioritize your creative vision"
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— TAKUMI, when you first met Mr. Nomura, what did you talk about?

Takumi Let's see. The reason I decided to become a game creator was because of Kingdom Hearts. You could say that Mr. Nomura is a key person in my life, and someone I greatly admire and respect, so I couldn't really do much more than greet him.

So, in order to break the ice, I told him that, as a fan, I had really wanted to play Final Fantasy Versus XIII. (laughs)

I wondered how Mr. Nomura felt about that as a creator, so I thought that I could get a sense of his thoughts through that topic.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44899105/756a740775b9949bce064f6268b28ce2fc12786a.jpg

Nomura When we met [that first time] we didn't talk about game development at all, did we? I think we talked about how I was easier to talk to than you thought.

—— (laughs) Even though he said that to you, I'm sure you were still very nervous, right, TAKUMI?

Takumi Yes, I was.

—— Well, Mr. Nomura is a legendary game creator that you had admired since childhood, so it stands to reason that you would be nervous. By the way, how old are you right now, TAKUMI?

Takumi 31.

—— You're very young! How do all of you feel about young game creators like TAKUMI?

Kando I feel that there is a large variety [of different young creators].

Nomura Thinking about myself, I was able to do the most in my 30s. So, TAKUMI, these next ten years will be very important for you.

—— Why do you think your thirties are so important, Mr. Nomura?

Nomura Because everything you experience in your twenties becomes of use to you in your thirties. Plus, you still have the energy to pull all-nighters. Now that I'm old, all-nighters aren't happening. (laughs)

Hirano Isn't it a bit too early to be calling yourself "old"?

Kando Well, we are right on the verge of retirement age.

Nomura We're at the point where [we're thinking], "How many more games can I get out before I retire?" In your thirties, you have stamina and enthusiasm, and you have many things you've seen and experienced. Because of that, you can pour your utmost into making what you want.

—— I'd like to hear if you have any advice for what TAKUMI and other young creators should do.

Nomura I might have some ulterior motives in saying this, but you'll gradually trend towards making things that aren't good, so focus on your creative vision.

It's important to keep the feelings of wanting to prioritize your creative vision and proving its validity with your own ability.

TAKUMI, please make REYNATIS 2!
————————————————————————————————————————————————————

—— We've talked about things directly related to REYNATIS, as well as things that are not today. Thank you all for giving us your thoughts. To wind things down, please give a message to the fans waiting for the results of your REYNATIS collaboration.

Kando Shibuya has been depicted in various ways, and NEO: The World Ends With You is a title that features Shibuya from our team's perspective.

I'm personally interested in seeing TAKUKMI's Shibuya, and I can't wait to play REYNATIS.

I want fans of NEO: The World Ends With You to see just how that Shibuya has found its way into REYNATIS.

Hirano I've personally already got to play a bit of it due to the collaboration with the main game, and I feel that the players will enjoy what's there.

I think anyone interested in REYNATIS is ok to keep their anticipation levels high.

Nomura This collaboration was born from TAKUMI's enthusiasm. We took on that enthusiasm and did everything we could to assist. I'm sure everyone will understand that we didn't take this on half-heartedly, so I'm truly hoping that it is well-received.

It would be great if fans of The World Ends With You fans enjoyed REYNATIS, and I would be very happy if REYNATIS fans became interested in The World Ends With You because of it.

Hirano That's right. Everyone, please check out the The World Ends With You games as well!

Takumi For this collaboration, we were able to overcome the hurdle of being in different companies and were able to make a good game thanks to everyone's collaborative efforts. I'm very grateful for that.

As a fan of the wonderful The World Ends With You games, and as a representative of those other fans, I thought about how happy I would be if something like this happened, and channeled that thought throughout the whole collaboration. I hope that everyone will enjoy it, along with REYNATIS.

Nomura If this game does well, I would like for TAKUMI to make a REYNATIS 2. Then, even better things might happen.

—— I have a feeling that because of this collaboration, more creators will come knocking on your door, Mr. Nomura. How do you feel about that?

Nomura So long as I'm around, feel free to knock. I can't say the same for after I retire, though. (laughs)

All (laughs)

Hirano We talked about TAKUMI's age a while ago. It's really rare for someone to be both a producer and a director at 31 years old, and to come to us with so much passion.

There might be other creators who feel hesitant to do something like that, so I think it shows just how valuable TAKUMI's talent is.

Takumi Thank you very much! A while ago, Mr. Nomura, you mentioned that it's not just about money and status, but also making something good. I hope that you continue to do just that.

Nomura Well, money is pretty important. (laughs)

All (laughs)

—— I don't think anyone believes that. (laughs) Thank you all very much for today!
